messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Elevated error rate and timeouts from inference-proxy in us-west-2a (AZ1a). ~30% of requests to g5 pools returning 5xx or timing out. Impacting production tenants. See: https://internal.status/redwood/2398765432

Tessa: ack — paging oncall. tagging @kai

kai: oncall here, pulling logs. initial look: proxy shows lots of TCP retransmits and ECONNRESET between frontend ELBs and inference hosts, spikes started ~13:02 UTC.

kai: running tcpdump on a affected host now, seeing repeated IP fragments and dropped packets when packet size > 1500. suspicious MTU/fragmentation.

kai: tcpdump snippet:
```
16:13:08.123456 IP hostA.12345 > hostB.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1501, ack 1, win 229, length 1500
16:13:08.123457 IP hostA > hostB: Frag 1/2: proto TCP, id 0x1a2b, fragoff 0
16:13:08.123458 IP hostA > hostB: Frag 2/2: proto TCP, id 0x1a2b, fragoff 185
```

riley-network: I see flaps on the ToR that handles AZ1a uplink — counters showing occasional path MTU blackholes after the kernel update rolled yesterday to the G5 fleet. Could be NIC offload/GSO/GRO interaction with newer switch firmware.

amanda: Customer impact: Prod inference SLAs for several customers degraded, error rates up ~12-20% for affected models. CS notified and we have an open bridge with a major customer.

kai: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily steer a fraction of traffic away from AZ1a to us-west-2b/d while we fix hosts. 2) disable large offloads (GSO/GRO/TSO) on affected hosts to avoid fragmentation, 3) roll a small config that shrinks default batch size on proxy to reduce large-packet generation.

kai: commands I'm running on the first batch (g5 nodes):
```
# disable offloads
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off
# enable MTU probing as safeguard
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
```

deploy-bot: Starting canary: routing-split apply — shift 10% traffic from us-west-2a -> us-west-2b for inference-proxy-route.

riley-network: routing shift at 13:23 UTC to 10%. Monitoring BGP and internal LB metrics.

kai: rolling disable-offload script to 30% of the G5 fleet in AZ1a. also pushing a runtime flag for inference-proxy: --max_batch_tokens=256 to reduce packet sizes from proxy.

tessa: coordinating with Support: we emailed top 5 impacted customers, posting note to status page.

riley-network: after initial 10% shift and first host fixes, 5xx rate dropped from ~30% -> 9% in the affected pools. packet drop counters on ToR reduced.

amanda: CS update: customer X reports partial recovery; still seeing spikes but degraded impact. They've requested ETA.

kai: ETA for full mitigation: finish offload disable across AZ1a (rolling), then validate at 60% traffic shift and progressively increase back. If stable, we'll re-enable offloads after firmware/kernel alignment.

deploy-bot: routing-split update — shifting additional 30% (total 40%) away from AZ1a.

riley-network: 40% shift complete, error rate down to ~4% overall. latency 95p also improving.

tessa: creating incident ticket INC-2398765432, severity: Sev2. adding owners: kai (lead), riley-network (network), amanda (customer comms).

kai: postmortem notes in brief: probable root cause is host kernel update that changed GSO/GRO handling + ToR firmware that doesn't handle large fragmented TCP consistently, causing path MTU blackholes for large inference payloads. Non-HTTP keepalive connections see fragmentation more.

kai: short-term actions: finish offload disable on AZ1a hosts, keep routing shift at 40% until 95th pctrl stable < baseline+20%. Notify infra for coordinated kernel/firmware rollback or vendor patch.

riley-network: will coordinate with cloud provider to validate ToR firmware and escalate if needed. Also scheduling a test harness to validate large-packet path.

amanda: posting status update to customers and support channels now. updating the status page: "Partial service degradation in us-west-2a; mitigation in progress."

kai: handing off active watch to night oncall @lex-oncall for followup and to continue rollouts. lex — I'm tagging the runbook and current commands in INC-2398765432. last status: 40% traffic shifted, error rate ~4%, continuing offload disables.

lex-oncall: ack, taking over watch. I'll coordinate with riley and amanda for oncall window.

tessa: thanks team. Follow-ups: schedule postmortem, add MTU/offload checks to host-upgrade playbook, create an automated smoke test that sends large-payload inference requests during every kernel upgrade.

kai: noted. adding to action items. closing active pager for now; will re-open if metrics regress. 

incident-bot: Pager cleared — no new alerts in the last 5m."
